name: TLE2426IP
title: TLE2426, TLE2426Y: rail-splitter precision virtual ground at one-half VI
summary: A three-terminal virtual ground that holds its output at exactly half of a 4 V to 40 V supply, built from a trimmed divider and a micropower buffer amplifier on one die. It sources or sinks about 20 mA with milliohm output impedance while drawing 170 µA, so a single-supply analog system gets a stiff signal ground without discrete op amps and resistors. The 8-pin versions add a noise-reduction pin for a filter capacitor. TLE2426IP is the industrial-grade (−40 °C to 85 °C) part in an 8-pin plastic DIP.

operation.text: A rail splitter: an on-chip precision resistor divider sets a point at half the input voltage and a micropower op amp, wired as a unity-gain buffer, drives that point onto OUT. The result is a low-impedance virtual ground for single-supply analog circuits that holds VO/VI at 0.5 while sourcing or sinking current.

Works from 4 V to 40 V on IN. Quiescent draw is 170 µA typical at VI = 5 V and stays below 280 µA across the full input range (400 µA maximum over 4 V to 40 V and full temperature range; 350 µA in the M grade's 12 V characteristics).

Sources and sinks 20 mA typical. Load regulation is −45 µV typical for 0 to −10 mA (sourcing) and +15 µV typical for 0 to +10 mA (sinking); output impedance is 7.5 mΩ typical. Negative IO is current out of OUT, positive IO is current into it.
Within 1 % initial output tolerance at a single 5 V or 12 V supply; within 3.6 % anywhere in the 4 V to 40 V range. Ripple rejection is beyond 12 bits.

Only the 8-pin D, JG and P packages bring out the divider midpoint as NOISE REDUCTION; the 3-lead LP package has no such pin. An external capacitor CNR on this pin cuts rms noise (10 Hz to 10 kHz) from 120 µV to 30 µV with 1 µF and lifts ripple rejection, which peaks near 98 dB around 20 kHz with 1 µF against about 6 dB flat without it (Figure 13).

OUT may be shorted to either supply rail indefinitely at or below 25 °C ambient, as long as supply voltage and temperature keep dissipation inside the package rating. Typical short-circuit current at 25 °C is 26 mA sinking and −47 mA sourcing at VI = 5 V, 31 mA and −70 mA at 12 V.

At VI = 5 V and 25 °C there is a band of load capacitance, roughly 0.0007 µF to 0.3 µF, in which the output is unstable once the output current rises above a threshold of about 2.7 mA to 7.5 mA in the positive (sinking) direction (Figure 17). Below and outside that region, including all negative (sourcing) currents shown, the output is stable.

C-suffix parts are characterized from 0 °C to 70 °C, I-suffix from −40 °C to 85 °C, and M-suffix from −55 °C to 125 °C. The guaranteed full-range output window widens with the grade: at VI = 5 V it is 2.475–2.525 V (C), 2.47–2.53 V (I) and 2.465–2.535 V (M).

The bare die behaves like the TLE2426C once assembled and is tested at 25 °C only. Its aluminium pads accept thermocompression or ultrasonic bonding; for die attach, a gold-silicon preform or conductive epoxy both work. OUT, COMMON and IN each have two pads, and both of each pair have to be bonded.

Tape-and-reel D and LP parts carry an R suffix: TLE2426CDR, TLE2426CLPR, TLE2426IDR, TLE2426ILPR. LP parts with straight leads ship in bulk only; formed-lead LP parts ship on tape and reel or in ammo pack.

A macromodel subcircuit named TLE2426 is published with node order filter (noise reduction), input, common, output, made for a 5 V supply. Its input divider is two 220 kΩ resistors from input to filter node and from filter node to common.
